If $0<\tau _0<\tau _1$, and $f$ is nonnegative, smooth, bounded, and has bounded spatial gradient, then \[ \int _{\tau _0}^{\tau _1}\int _{M_\infty \times \{ -\tau \} } \mathcal D f\tau ^{-n/2}e^{-l_\infty } \, d\vol _{g_\infty }\, d\tau \geq 0. \]
Proof

\sketch ↗ claim:absolute-convergence-weighted-distribution ↗ claim:absolute-convergence-laplacian-term ↗ cor:weighted-distribution-nonnegative Test Corollary 9 against $f\psi _k$, where $\psi _k$ are uniformly Lipschitz distance cutoffs. The two absolute-convergence results justify passage to the limit.
